minutes.headline: Senior center elevator project ruled out as infeasible; committee to seek input on 10-year senior needs plan
minutes.summary: This Council on Aging meeting was mostly informational: reports on caregiver support programming, a heavily booked September activity calendar, a Unitil solar-interconnection cost complaint, and an update that installing an elevator (Lula Lift) at the senior center is not feasible due to space, code and cost constraints, with porch screening floated as a cheaper alternative. The board also discussed the town's master plan (including a push to make assisted living a formal goal rather than a "nice to have"), agreed to draft a warrant article to get the town to formally approve the 41A tax deferral program, and adjourned after routine reports on kiosk completion, sand-for-seniors delivery, and kitchen staffing.

what_happened.line: Installing an elevator at the senior center was ruled out as infeasible on space, code and cost grounds; porch screening was raised as a cheaper alternative but not decided.
The committee agreed to seek member ideas for a 10-year senior needs section of the town's master plan, due back by October 1.

The board agreed to draft a warrant article asking the town to formally adopt the 41A property tax deferral program, after a resident reportedly lost a deferral this year because the town has not formally approved it.
The chair agreed to draft a letter about a resident's complaint over Unitil's solar-interconnection fees, to be sent once the select board liaison returns to sign on.
A decision on making trial Friday closures and evening hours permanent was postponed to the September meeting.

why_it_matters: The elevator decision affects whether the senior center becomes more accessible to residents with mobility limitations, and what replaces it will need its own funding and approval.
The 41A warrant article, if it advances, would give seniors a formal, town-approved way to defer property taxes rather than relying on inconsistent practice.
The master plan's senior needs section and the assisted-living goal will shape what the town commits to planning for seniors over the next decade.
